title: Owner Auto Policy Rating Bulletin — Occasional-Operator Relativity for a Driver Whose Exclusion Is Lifted
content:
**Occasional-operator relativity.** Under the company's filed driver rating, the lift share of a driver whose named driver exclusion is lifted on the Owner Auto Policy is rated with an occasional-operator relativity. The share is multiplied before it is rounded to the cent. The relativity compares the rated drivers on the term, once the lift is made, with the term's recorded vehicle count.

**Counting the rated drivers.** Every rated driver other than the named insured, including a driver rated when the term was bound, is carried by a driver-added entry. The rated drivers are counted as follows:
- the named insured;
- plus one for each driver-added entry on the term;
- less one for each driver-removed or driver-excluded entry that records a prior status of rated;
- plus the driver being lifted.

| Rated drivers once the lift is made, against the vehicles on the term | Relativity |
|---|---|
| exceed the vehicles by two or more | 0.7 (the lifted driver, the last added, rated as an occasional operator) |
| exceed the vehicles by one | 0.8 |
| any other count | 1 |

**Hypothetical counts on a two-vehicle term.**

| Driver-added entries | Rated drivers removed or excluded | Rated count with the lifted driver | Relativity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | 3 | 0.8 |
| 2 | 0 | 4 | 0.7 |
| 1 | 1 | 2 | 1 |
